data.title: Last fifty years of integer linear programming: Recent practical advances (2024)
data.author: teleforce
data.article_summary: 本文回顾了过去五十年混合整数线性规划（MILP）的进展，重点关注实际应用和近期计算性能的提升。MILP已成为运筹学的核心，现代求解器能高效解决十年前无法处理的问题，广泛应用于交通、物流、供应链、金融等领域。文章聚焦于分支定界法（branch-and-cut）、Dantzig-Wolfe分解和Benders分解三大方法，总结了关键研究成果，并指出MILP领域仍面临的挑战和未来研究方向。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：商业ILP求解器（如Gurobi）为何优于开源求解器，及其在实际应用中的表现和成本问题。

不同观点：
• [aquafox] 认为ILP问题由于其NP难性质，难以找到通用的高效解法，商业求解器通过大量针对特定子问题的启发式算法实现性能提升，而这些方法未进入公共领域。
• [dcminter] 通过自身经历说明算法和硬件的进步带来了巨大的性能提升，特别是在资源分配工具中，这种提升尤为明显，问题解决时间从长期运行缩短到几分钟。
• [tormeh] 提出实际应用中数值优化的实现可能因数据问题（如信任、数据质量）而失败，最终决策可能依赖于个人经验和直觉。
• [pradn] 引用研究数据，指出自1988年以来，LP求解器的速度提升了3300倍，结合硬件提升，整体性能提高了数百万倍，并提出在不同计算子领域中比较算法和硬件提升的必要性。
• [djoldman] 关注Gurobi的高昂价格，询问具体定价细节。
• [FabHK] 通过历史对比，说明自1990年代以来，求解LP问题的时间大幅缩短，现代MILP求解器的性能提升显著。
• [beret4breakfast] 认为目前基于ML/AI的方法在解决ILP等优化问题上效果不佳，实际应用中更高效的方法仍是运筹学（OR）方法，并分享了自己在调度优化中使用进化算法的经验。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了商业求解器Gurobi的高性能和昂贵价格，以及算法和硬件进步对求解速度的巨大影响。
• 实际应用中，数值优化的实现可能面临数据质量和信任问题，导致最终决策依赖于人工判断。
• 讨论中还涉及了ML/AI方法在ILP问题上的应用现状，目前看来这些方法尚不足以替代商业求解器。
• 历史对比和性能提升的数据为理解商业求解器的优势提供了量化支持。

Abstract
en
Mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) has become a cornerstone of operations research. This is driven by the enhanced efficiency of modern solvers, which can today find globally optimal solutions within seconds for problems that were out of reach a decade ago. The versatility of these solvers allowed successful applications in many areas, such as transportation, logistics, supply chain management, revenue management, finance, telecommunications, and manufacturing. Despite the impressive success already obtained, many challenges remain, and MILP is still a very active field.
This article provides an overview of the most significant results achieved in advancing the MILP solution methods. Given the immense literature on this topic, we made deliberate choices to focus on computational aspects and recent practical performance improvements, emphasizing research that reports computational experiments. We organize our survey into three main parts, dedicated to branch-and-cut methods, Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition, and Benders decomposition. The paper concludes by highlighting ongoing challenges and future opportunities in MILP research.

data.title: How to Build Conscious Machines
data.author: hardmaru
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：意识的本质及其在人工智能和哲学中的解释

不同观点：
• [AIorNot] 认为意识是一种主观体验，无法通过物理理论完全解释。即使我们能够关联神经活动和思想，但神经活动本身并不是思想。该评论质疑任何物理意识理论能否真正解释意识现象。
• [talkingtab] 关注实际应用，特别是如何构建有意识的机器。该评论质疑文章是否提供了可操作的指导，并指出AI中的“知识”和“能力”之间的区别。同时，提出复杂适应系统（CAS）可能具有意识，例如RIP路由协议。
• [trod1234] 反对创造有意识的机器，认为这是浪费资源。他们认为，人类已经有能力通过生育孩子来创造有意识的生命，而创造其他有意识的存在没有实际意义，并可能导致道德问题。
• [esafak] 简要介绍了论文中的五阶段意识层次，并指出论文声称解决了意识的难题，但未详细说明如何评估某个有机体属于哪个阶段。该评论还提到了IIT（整合信息理论）作为可能的评估方法。
• [Avicebron] 对文章中提到的多种理论和解释表示怀疑，认为其没有充分论证。
• [qgin] 认为我们只能知道自己有意识，但无法知道他人是否有意识。我们假设他人有意识是为了获得同样的礼貌对待。
• [disambiguation] 质疑论文中对“基质依赖”的处理，认为作者没有充分解释或证明为何可以忽略基质独立性。该评论指出，生物智能的进展都依赖于相同的基质，因此假设基质独立性并不合理。
• [gcanyon] 提出是否需要在AI中实现意识以达到特定目标的问题。该评论认为，某些任务可能不需要意识，而意识可能是高度智能系统的副产品。
• [catigula] 认为当前关于意识的理论都不完美，推荐了泛心论和Russellian monism作为可能的理论方向。该评论指出，意识问题被称为“难题”是有原因的。
• [canadiantim] 质疑论文中对“感受性（qualia）”的处理，认为论文假设感受性可以被进一步分解，但没有提供证据。该评论认为，感受性是不可还原的基本元素。
• [briian] 提出通过深入理解人脑来改进AI系统的可能性，指出人工神经网络和大型语言模型都受到人脑结构的启发。
• [nativeit] 以幽默的方式表达了对不同繁殖选择方式的尊重。
• [m3kw9] 质疑如何定义和测试意识。
• [PunchTornado] 认为文章没有提出新的观点，许多内容在Chalmers和Dennett等人的工作中已经被更深入地讨论过。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于意识是否可以被物理理论解释，以及是否应该或能够创造有意识的机器。
• 另一个重要讨论点是感受性（qualia）是否可以被进一步分解，以及如何评估某个有机体的意识层次。
• 实际应用和伦理问题也被多次提及，特别是在资源分配和创造有意识的存在的道德性方面。

data.title: Meta-analysis of three different notions of software complexity
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary:
这篇文章总结了三种软件复杂性的概念：

1. **Rich Hickey的复杂性概念**：Hickey认为简单性意味着“单一性”——一个事物应具有“一个折叠/辫子、一个角色、一个任务、一个概念、一个维度”，不应混杂其他元素。他区分了“简单”和“容易”，前者是客观的，而后者是主观的，依赖于个人的判断。Hickey强调，简单性有助于易于理解、易于更改、调试和灵活性。他还对比了“交织”（complect）和“组合”（compose），主张避免交织以减少复杂性。

2. **John Ousterhout的复杂性概念**：Ousterhout认为复杂性是任何让系统难以理解和修改的结构，并强调“显而易见性”是系统设计的重要目标。显而易见性意味着开发者能快速理解代码并做出正确修改，减少认知负担。复杂性主要来源于依赖性和模糊性，依赖性无法完全消除，但应尽量减少。

3. **Zach Tellman的复杂性概念**：文章未详细展开，但强调复杂性常源于系统各部分的相互作用和时间维度。

这三种观点都旨在通过减少交织和依赖，使软件更易于理解和维护。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件复杂性的定义与衡量

不同观点：
• [perrygeo] 支持Tellman的观点，认为简单性是软件与人类期望之间的契合，具有主观性。他认为简单性与软件在人脑中形成的预测模型相关，而不是单纯的技术指标如数量或交织度。这种观点强调主观体验和人对系统的理解。
• [burakemir] 认为在特定场景（如处理紧急系统故障）中，Tellman的主观视角可能不适用。在这种情况下，客观的改进和减少系统理解难度更为重要。他指出，虽然主观视角有其价值，但在某些实际操作情境中，更需要客观的标准。
• [_benton] 更倾向于Ousterhout的观点，认为其更为具体。同时指出“依赖”这一术语在不同情境下可能具有不同含义，并提出通过假设的数量来衡量复杂性。
• [amelius] 提到正交性（orthogonality）在讨论中被忽略，暗示这是另一种衡量软件复杂性的重要角度。
• [readthenotes1] 引用研究文章，指出代码行数（LOC）与多种复杂性度量高度相关，认为简单关注代码行数也能接近复杂性度量的结果。
• [adityaathalye] 用火箭方程比喻软件复杂性，强调复杂性是动态多维的，并通过时间和空间维度来解释。他提到行为对复杂性的影响，并指出即使复杂的静态系统也可能比动态系统更简单。
• [0xbadcafebee] 提出软件讨论可以分为哲学、科学和功能三个层次。哲学层次关注理解和解释，科学层次追求客观和共识，而功能层次则是日常开发实践。他认为大多数开发者主要关注功能层次，而非哲学或科学讨论。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于简单性/复杂性是主观的还是客观的。部分评论者（如perrygeo和burakemir）对主观和客观视角进行了对比，并讨论了不同情境下的适用性。
• 一些评论者（如_benton和amelius）提到了术语定义和未被讨论的概念（如正交性），扩展了讨论的范围。
• 技术性度量（如LOC和 McCabe 循环复杂度）在复杂性讨论中的角色也被提及，强调了简单度量指标的实际应用价值。
• 0xbadcafebee的评论为讨论提供了一个框架，帮助理解不同层次的软件讨论如何相互作用和区别。

44274696.article_content:
A meta-analysis of three different notions of software complexity
I want to discuss three different notions of software complexity:
Rich Hickey’s notion of complexity, as explained in his talk
Simple Made Easy
.
John Ousterhout’s notion of complexity, as explained in his book
A Philosophy of Software Design
.
Zach Tellman’s notion of complexity, as explained in his newsletter
Explaining Software Design
.
I’ve picked these three because I’ve found them to be at least somewhat coherent,
and the former two to be (relatively) well-known;
this blog post is not meant to be exhaustive
of all different definitions of complexity that have been
offered over the years.
The definitions summarized
(Formatting note: exact quotes are taken from the above-mentioned work.)
Hickey complexity
Hickey defines something as being simple as having some kind of oneness - he uses the phrases “one fold/braid, one role, one task, one concept, one dimension.” Hickey states, “When you’re looking for something simple, you want to see it have focus in these areas. You don’t want to see it combining things.”
Hickey contrasts ‘easy’ with ‘simple’. For ‘easy’, the central idea is proximity – in terms of access (e.g. already having something be installed, being able to easily install something), in terms of existing skills and capabilities, and so on. Hickey points out that ‘easy’ is subjective, because it is relative to the person making the judgement.
As one example here, Hickey states that the parentheses in Clojure are hard (i.e. the opposite of easy) but simple, and that
it is users’ responsibility
to fix this.
On the other hand, Hickey states that this notion of simplicity is objective, “we can probably go and look and see, I don’t see any connections, I don’t see where this twists with something else.”
Hickey stresses the difference between simplicity and low cardinality (“But not: One instance, one operation.”). He points out that the important thing is “lack of interleaving, not cardinality.”
Hickey sums up his argument against complexity as follows:
“We can only hope to make reliable those things we can understand”
“We can only consider a few things at a time”
“Intertwined things must be considered together”
“Complexity undermines understanding”
According to Hickey, simplicity has the following benefits:
Ease of understanding
Ease of change
Easier debugging
Flexibility

44274696.article_summary:
这篇文章总结了三种软件复杂性的概念：

1. **Rich Hickey的复杂性概念**：Hickey认为简单性意味着“单一性”——一个事物应具有“一个折叠/辫子、一个角色、一个任务、一个概念、一个维度”，不应混杂其他元素。他区分了“简单”和“容易”，前者是客观的，而后者是主观的，依赖于个人的判断。Hickey强调，简单性有助于易于理解、易于更改、调试和灵活性。他还对比了“交织”（complect）和“组合”（compose），主张避免交织以减少复杂性。

2. **John Ousterhout的复杂性概念**：Ousterhout认为复杂性是任何让系统难以理解和修改的结构，并强调“显而易见性”是系统设计的重要目标。显而易见性意味着开发者能快速理解代码并做出正确修改，减少认知负担。复杂性主要来源于依赖性和模糊性，依赖性无法完全消除，但应尽量减少。

3. **Zach Tellman的复杂性概念**：文章未详细展开，但强调复杂性常源于系统各部分的相互作用和时间维度。

这三种观点都旨在通过减少交织和依赖，使软件更易于理解和维护。
44274696.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件复杂性的定义与衡量

不同观点：
• [perrygeo] 支持Tellman的观点，认为简单性是软件与人类期望之间的契合，具有主观性。他认为简单性与软件在人脑中形成的预测模型相关，而不是单纯的技术指标如数量或交织度。这种观点强调主观体验和人对系统的理解。
• [burakemir] 认为在特定场景（如处理紧急系统故障）中，Tellman的主观视角可能不适用。在这种情况下，客观的改进和减少系统理解难度更为重要。他指出，虽然主观视角有其价值，但在某些实际操作情境中，更需要客观的标准。
• [_benton] 更倾向于Ousterhout的观点，认为其更为具体。同时指出“依赖”这一术语在不同情境下可能具有不同含义，并提出通过假设的数量来衡量复杂性。
• [amelius] 提到正交性（orthogonality）在讨论中被忽略，暗示这是另一种衡量软件复杂性的重要角度。
• [readthenotes1] 引用研究文章，指出代码行数（LOC）与多种复杂性度量高度相关，认为简单关注代码行数也能接近复杂性度量的结果。
• [adityaathalye] 用火箭方程比喻软件复杂性，强调复杂性是动态多维的，并通过时间和空间维度来解释。他提到行为对复杂性的影响，并指出即使复杂的静态系统也可能比动态系统更简单。
• [0xbadcafebee] 提出软件讨论可以分为哲学、科学和功能三个层次。哲学层次关注理解和解释，科学层次追求客观和共识，而功能层次则是日常开发实践。他认为大多数开发者主要关注功能层次，而非哲学或科学讨论。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于简单性/复杂性是主观的还是客观的。部分评论者（如perrygeo和burakemir）对主观和客观视角进行了对比，并讨论了不同情境下的适用性。
• 一些评论者（如_benton和amelius）提到了术语定义和未被讨论的概念（如正交性），扩展了讨论的范围。
• 技术性度量（如LOC和 McCabe 循环复杂度）在复杂性讨论中的角色也被提及，强调了简单度量指标的实际应用价值。
• 0xbadcafebee的评论为讨论提供了一个框架，帮助理解不同层次的软件讨论如何相互作用和区别。

data.title: How multiplication is defined in Peano arithmetic
data.author: nill0
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了递归原则在数学中的重要性和其常被误解的现象，特别是在自然数的加法和乘法定义中的应用。作者指出，尽管递归在现代数学中无处不在，但很多人，包括一些学生和维基百科的解释，常常未能正确理解和阐明这一概念。文章特别强调，乘法并不是简单重复的加法，这种错误的表述在基础数学教育中尤为常见。作者认为，即使在教学中为了简化而省略一些细节，也不应向学生传达错误的信息。递归原则是一个关键的存在性断言，用于从后继函数构造加法，并从加法定义乘法，缺乏这个原则就无法正确定义这些运算。文章最后呼吁对递归原则的重视，并解释其在数学中的必要性和应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于“乘法作为重复加法”与递归定义的争议，以及在不同数学背景下递归和加法的定义与应用。

不同观点：
• [grogers] 认为在编程中，迭代和递归在功能上是等价的，可以相互转换。因此，他不理解为什么在数学中“乘法作为重复加法”的定义会被批评，觉得这种定义没有问题。
• [nrds] 指出文章中关于递归与无穷相关的论述是基于集合论基础的，但这不是唯一的视角。在如Coq、Lean和Agda等证明助手的类型理论中，递归与有限的结构密切相关，并且在这些背景下，递归是一个定义明确的计算过程。
• [BoiledCabbage] 对比了两种不同的加法递归定义，提出了关于两种定义是否存在显著差异的问题。第一种定义是逐步减少b并加到总和上，第二种定义则是将b减少的部分加到a上。
• [im3w1l] 探讨了在没有递归公理的情况下，所谓的“超自然数”的可能性。他描述了在没有递归公理时，可能存在的不同数集结构（如N的副本、Z的副本等），并讨论了在这种情况下的加法定义及其潜在结果。他认为这种定义可能会产生一致但不太有趣或有用的扩展。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是递归定义在不同数学背景下的应用和解释。一些人认为递归在某些背景下是有限且明确的，而文章中提到的与无穷相关的论述并不必要。
• 关于加法定义的具体形式，BoiledCabbage提出的两种定义方式引起了对其实际差异的讨论。
• im3w1l的扩展讨论展示了在没有递归公理的情况下，加法定义可以有不同的一致性扩展，这为理解递归和加法提供了新的视角。

44274854.article_content:
A familiar joke in mathematical logic (the field I worked in for the first twenty years of my career) is the following hypothetical entry in a mathematical dictionary:
Recursion
See “Recursion”.
Though recursion is ubiquitous in modern mathematics, even at the most basic level of the analysis of the arithmetic of natural numbers, it is a subtle concept, easily misunderstood. At its heart is the always problematic step from the finite to the infinite.  Having taught set theory and the foundations of mathematics for many years at various universities, I long ago learned that many students never do fully grasp it.
Many sources gloss over it. For example, the
Wikipedia entry
for the Peano Axioms for the natural numbers, which on the whole is pretty good, refers to “
recursion
”
to justify its definitions of addition and multiplication on the natural numbers, but the Wikipedia page it links to punts when it comes to properly explaining the all important Recursion Principle, let alone proving it (the set-theoretic Recursion Theorem), giving a sketch proof of uniqueness (easy) but not the crucial existence part (which many people find tricky). [My comments refer to the pages when I accessed them on October 31, 2011.]
The widespread lack of appreciation for the Recursion Principle (it’s a principle you
use
when you are developing Peano arithmetic, a theorem you
prove
when you are doing set theory) lay behind many of the erroneous comments I received in response to my series of articles on multiplication not being repeated addition (not even on the natural numbers). Those articles appeared on
MAA Online
in
June 2008
,
July-August 2008
,
September 2008
, and
January 2011
.
If you really understand the Recursion Principle, which is what is
required
in order to construct addition from the successor function and to define multiplication from addition, then you will know that addition is
not
repeated successor (though oddly, no one ever claimed that to be the case) and multiplication is
not
repeated addition.
ASIDE:
This is not an article about mathematics education. How teachers introduce addition and multiplication is another issue. I am not, repeat not, suggesting we teach recursion in the K-12 system. My complaint throughout that previous exchange was that, whatever and however we teach in our schools, we should not be stating things that are flat wrong. In this column I want to explain the recursion principle, its importance, its power, its need in mathematics, and how it is used, so you too will know why it is flat wrong to tell kids that multiplication is repeated addition. Remember, even if you don’t see the purpose of all the mathematical navel-inspection that led to the formulation of the principle, some of the students in your class may well find themselves wanting or needing to understand it in a few years time. While it is often pedagogically wise to say less than the whole truth, we should not lie to our students.
Okay, I’m back off my pulpit. The Recursion Principle is a rabbit-out-of-the-hat existence assertion. When used to construct addition from the successor function in Peano arithmetic, it tells you that there is a function from NxN to N that, lo-and-behold, can in any specific instance (i.e., for any pair of specific natural number arguments) be calculated by repeatedly applying the successor function a fixed number of times. Likewise, when the recursion principle is used to construct multiplication from addition in Peano arithmetic, it tells you that there is a function from NxN to N that, again wonder-of-wonders, can in any specific instance (i.e., for any pair of specific natural number arguments) be calculated by repeatedly adding a fixed number of times.
You need to invoke the Recursion Principle in order to obtain addition and multiplication because without it you just don’t get those functions. Period.
Let’s see how the Wikipedia entry I referred to earlier handles the Peano constructions of addition and multiplication.
(click image for full size)
If you read that Wikipedia account carefully, you will see that it does not actually tell you how to define addition or multiplication. Rather it tells you the properties those functions will have
once they have been defined
. The closest you get to an indication of how the two functions are defined is that word “recursively”, which as I noted earlier, links to another Wikipedia page that also does not tell you how the function is defined.
The definition is actually not difficult, provided you are used to working in abstract set theory. But since most people are not, authors typically leave it out, an instance where saying less than the whole truth is, in my view, justifiable. (Though I think they should explicitly note that what is being missed out is fundamental and important.)

data.title: Inside the Apollo “8-Ball” FDAI (Flight Director / Attitude Indicator)
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了阿波罗登月任务中用于显示飞船姿态的FDAI（飞行总监/姿态指示器）的运作原理。FDAI通过一个被称为"8-ball"的球体显示飞船的姿态，球体可以绕三轴（滚转、俯仰和偏航）旋转。该仪器还通过三根黄色指针指示 astronauts 应如何操纵飞船，另有三根指针显示飞船的旋转速度。FDAI内部使用三个马达分别控制球体绕三轴的旋转，球体在“赤道”处牢固连接，并通过外部壳体实现第三轴的旋转。Lunar Module 拥有两个FDAI，一个供指挥官使用，另一个供登月舱驾驶员使用，每个FDAI可以从多个来源获取数据并显示姿态信息和旋转速率。仪表通过不同的开关选择显示模式和数据源，并由阿波罗制导计算机等设备提供误差指示。

44277051.article_content:
During the Apollo flights to the Moon, the astronauts observed the spacecraft's orientation on a special instrument
called the FDAI (Flight Director / Attitude Indicator).
This instrument showed the spacecraft's attitude—its orientation—by rotating a ball.
This ball was nicknamed the "8-ball" because it was black (albeit only on one side).
The instrument also acted as a flight director, using three yellow needles to indicate how the astronauts should maneuver
the spacecraft. Three more pointers showed how fast the spacecraft was rotating.
An Apollo FDAI (Flight Director/Attitude Indicator) with the case removed. This FDAI is on its side to avoid crushing the needles.
Since the spacecraft rotates along three axes (roll, pitch, and yaw), the ball also rotates along three axes.
It's not obvious how the ball can rotate to an arbitrary orientation while remaining attached.
In this article, I look inside an FDAI from Apollo that was repurposed for a Space Shuttle simulator
1
and explain how it operates. (Spoiler: the ball mechanism is firmly attached
at the "equator" and rotates in two axes. What you see is two hollow shells around the ball mechanism that spin around the third axis.)
The FDAI in Apollo
For the missions to the Moon, the Lunar Module had two FDAIs, as shown below: one on the left for the Commander (Neil Armstrong in Apollo 11) and
one on the right for the Lunar Module Pilot (Buzz Aldrin in Apollo 11).
With their size and central positions, the FDAIs dominate the instrument panel, a sign of their importance.
(The Command Module for Apollo also had two FDAIs, but with a different design; I won't discuss them here.
2
)
The instrument panel in the Lunar Module. From
Apollo 15 Lunar Module
, NASA, S71-40761. If you're looking for the DSKY, it is in the bottom center, just out of the picture.
Each Lunar Module FDAI could display inputs from multiple sources, selected by switches on the panel.
3
The ball could display attitude from either the
Inertial Measurement Unit
or from the backup Abort Guidance System, selected by the "ATTITUDE MON" toggle switch next to either FDAI.
The pitch attitude could also be supplied by an electromechanical unit called ORDEAL (Orbital Rate Display Earth And Lunar)
that simulates a circular orbit.
The error indications came from the Apollo Guidance Computer, the Abort Guidance System, the landing radar,
or the rendezvous radar (controlled by the "RATE/ERROR MON" switches).
The pitch, roll, and yaw rate displays were driven by the Rate Gyro Assembly (RGA).
The rate indications were scaled by a switch below the FDAI, selecting 25°/sec or 5°/sec.
The FDAI mechanism
The ball inside the indicator shows rotation around three axes.
I'll first explain these axes in the context of an aircraft, since the axes of a spacecraft are more arbitrary.
4
The roll axis indicates the aircraft's angle if it rolls side-to-side along its axis of flight, raising one wing
and lowering the other.
Thus, the indicator shows the tilt of the horizon as the aircraft rolls.
The pitch axis indicates the aircraft's angle if it pitches up or down, with the indicator showing the horizon
moving down or up in response.
Finally, the yaw axis indicates the compass direction that the aircraft is heading,
changing as the aircraft turns left or right.
(A typical aircraft attitude indicator omits yaw.)

44277051.article_summary: 本文介绍了阿波罗登月任务中用于显示飞船姿态的FDAI（飞行总监/姿态指示器）的运作原理。FDAI通过一个被称为"8-ball"的球体显示飞船的姿态，球体可以绕三轴（滚转、俯仰和偏航）旋转。该仪器还通过三根黄色指针指示 astronauts 应如何操纵飞船，另有三根指针显示飞船的旋转速度。FDAI内部使用三个马达分别控制球体绕三轴的旋转，球体在“赤道”处牢固连接，并通过外部壳体实现第三轴的旋转。Lunar Module 拥有两个FDAI，一个供指挥官使用，另一个供登月舱驾驶员使用，每个FDAI可以从多个来源获取数据并显示姿态信息和旋转速率。仪表通过不同的开关选择显示模式和数据源，并由阿波罗制导计算机等设备提供误差指示。

data.title: We investigated Amsterdam's attempt to build a 'fair' fraud detection model
data.author: troelsSteegin
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了阿姆斯特丹市开发的一种机器学习模型，旨在识别需要进一步调查的福利申请。该模型使用了一种名为可解释提升机（EBM）的算法，通过分析申请者的行为和特征来预测“调查价值”，并生成风险评分。尽管模型没有直接使用性别或种族等敏感信息，但仍可能通过其他变量间接关联到特定群体。文章指出，尽管阿姆斯特丹在开发过程中努力确保模型的透明和公平，但其他地方如鹿特丹和法国社会保障机构在类似系统中忽视了对偏见的审查，导致对弱势群体的歧视。文章还提到，欧盟和纽约等地已开始通过立法限制高风险AI的使用，但构建公平的AI工具仍面临复杂挑战。最终，文章强调了在AI决策中实现公平的现实困难和持续努力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：模型公平性与偏差问题，特别是在处理人口统计群体和受保护特征时的取舍与挑战

不同观点：
• [tbrownaw] 认为模型设计者知道特征可能与人口统计群体相关，从而成为代理变量，导致不同公平定义之间的权衡。例如，关注减少基于种族/国籍的差异可能会在其他维度上表现更差。这种取舍是不可避免的。
• [thatguymike] 赞扬阿姆斯特丹的项目，认为他们在无法达到伦理标准时选择不部署模型，这是一种负责任的做法，应该在世界上更多地推广。
• [dannykwells] 提出是否可以为每个群体训练不同的模型，以保证平等对待。这种方法可以确保每个群体内部的公平性，但未讨论整体模型性能和复杂性问题。
• [GardenLetter27] 认为模型使用与人口统计特征相关的代理变量是符合贝叶斯法则的，而不是种族主义。这表明从统计学角度看，使用相关变量是合理的。
• [3abiton] 对城市在重新分析时无法完全复制数据和结果表示担忧，暗示实验的可信度可能受到影响，质疑是否有适当的系统和专业人员参与。
• [tomp] 指出模型公平性问题在其他领域同样存在，例如篮球或马拉松表现，不同群体的差异是自然的，而非不公平。

补充讨论：
• [bananaquant] 批评模型的准确性低，认为其表现仅比随机选择稍好，改进 marginal，不适合高风险场景。
• [wongarsu] 强调由于缺乏真实基础，评估新模型的无偏性是困难的。旧过程的不公正使得新模型也难以避免偏见，导致在不同偏差指标间的权衡和不确定性。
• [Jimmc414] 指出减少一种偏差（假阳性率）的同时增加另一种偏差（假发现率）是数学上的现实，训练基于过去人类决策的模型不可避免地会引入现有偏差。
• [ncruces] 认为唯一公平的方式可能是完全随机，暗示在复杂社会问题中实现算法公平可能不切实际。
• [octo888] 建议在标题中加入“福利”，以更准确描述模型应用的背景。
• [LorenPechtel] 质疑过度关注“公平”而忽视实际效果，认为应优先最小化假阳性和假阴性，而不是仅仅关注公平性。
• [BonoboIO] 批评文章缺乏关于系统实际捕捉欺诈的有效性数据，如真阳性率、召回率和财务追回情况，认为文章更多是道德展示，而非实际效果证明。
• [zeroCalories] 询问“reweighing demographics”的具体含义，关注模型如何在不同人口统计中表现良好，暗示应努力确保模型对所有群体的公平性。

争议焦点：
• 模型公平性与准确性之间的权衡：是否应为了减少某些偏差而接受整体性能下降。
• 使用与人口统计相关的代理变量的合理性：从统计学角度（贝叶斯法则）合理，但从伦理和社会公平角度可能存在争议。
• 旧数据和决策不公正对新模型的影响：如何在没有真实基础的情况下评估和确保模型的无偏性。

The Limits of Ethical AI

How the model works
Training the Model
Fairness Definitions
The City’s First Model
The City’s ‘Debiased’ Model
The Debiased Model is Deployed in a Pilot
Fairness Tradeoffs
Model Performance
Technical Details
Limitations
For the past four years, Lighthouse has investigated welfare fraud detection algorithms deployed in five European countries. Our investigations have found evidence that these systems discriminated against vulnerable groups with oftentimes steep consequences for people’s lives.
Governments and companies deploying these systems often show little regard for the biases they perpetrate against vulnerable groups. The city of Rotterdam told us that it had never run code designed to test whether its model was disproportionately flagging vulnerable groups. France’s social security agency, CNAF, confirmed to us that it had never audited its model for bias.
In January of 2023, three months before publishing our investigation into Rotterdam’s risk scoring algorithm, we sent a public records request to the city of Amsterdam, one of Europe’s most progressive capitals. Among other things, we asked for documents, code and data relating to a similar system Amsterdam had been developing. Given that we had fought over a year to obtain these types of material in other investigations, we were surprised when the city immediately complied with our request.
The materials disclosed by the city were related to a machine learning model it was developing in order to predict which of the city’s residents were most likely to have submitted an incorrect application for welfare. At the time of our public records request, the model was still in development. The overall development goal for the model, according to the city’s internal documentation, was to have fewer welfare applicants investigated, but a higher share of those investigated rejected. Internal documents also emphasized two other aims: avoid bias against vulnerable groups, and outperform human caseworkers.
After reading through the documentation, it quickly became clear to us why the city had been so forthcoming. The city had gone to significant lengths in order to develop a model that was transparent and treated vulnerable groups fairly.
We wanted to investigate whether the city of Amsterdam had succeeded in developing a fair model. Over the course of eight months, we ran a series of our own tests on the model and data containing real world outcomes for people flagged as suspicious by the model. When it came to the outcome data, the city ran our own tests locally and returned aggregate results in order to comply with European data protection laws.
The past five years have seen a number of regulatory efforts to reign in harmful uses of AI. The EU AI Act, passed in 2024, will require AI systems deemed “high risk” to be registered with the European Commission. In New York City, employers have been prohibited from screening employees using AI without conducting bias audits since July 2023. Meanwhile, the private sector, academics and multilateral institutions have produced a number of responsible AI frameworks. In taking on this investigation, we wanted to look ahead and understand the thorny reality of building a fair AI tool that makes consequential decisions about people’s lives.
The code and data underlying our analysis can be found on our
Github
.
How the model works
The City of Amsterdam’s model aimed to identify applications for further investigation. Staff members check for applications that contain mistakes and redirect any concerning applications to an investigator. The model is designed to replicate this first screening.
A flagged application is not automatically rejected. However, investigators are empowered to request a beneficiary’s bank statements, summon them for meetings, and even visit their homes. Past reporting, including our own, has shown how these investigations can be a stressful or even traumatising experience.
The model uses a type of algorithm called an Explainable Boosting Machine (EBM). EBMs prioritize explainability — the degree to which an AI algorithm is understandable instead of being a confusing “black box” of abstract mathematical processes. Amsterdam’s EBM model predicts ‘investigation worthiness’ based on variables that measure welfare applicants’ behavior and characteristics, features.
Model predictions are based on 15 features. None of these features explicitly referred to an applicant’s gender or racial background, as well as other demographic characteristics protected by anti-discrimination law. But the model designers were aware that features could be correlated with demographic groups in a way that would make them proxies.

data.title: Have a damaged painting? Restore it in just hours with an AI-generated “mask”
data.author: WithinReason
data.article_summary: 麻省理工学院的研究生Alex Kachkine开发了一种使用数字构造膜物理修复原始画作的新方法。该方法通过打印极薄的聚合物膜，形成一个可以对齐并粘贴到画作上的“面具”，以覆盖和修复受损区域，且该膜可以轻松移除。这种技术可以在几个小时内完成传统修复方法需要数周甚至更长时间的工作。例如，Kachkine在3.5小时内修复了一幅15世纪的油画，而传统方法可能需要更久。同时，数字记录可以保存修复细节，供未来修复者参考。不过，Kachkine也强调，任何修复都应与了解画作历史和来源的保护专家协商，以确保修复的伦理性和适当性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：艺术品修复中的技术应用（特别是AI）及其伦理问题

不同观点：
• **Daub**：对艺术品修复持批评态度，认为过去的修复项目往往造成了对艺术品的破坏。他举例提到西斯廷教堂天花板的修复项目，认为选择了错误的假设（即米开朗基罗没有对壁画进行任何修正），从而破坏了原作。他还提到维多利亚时代对雕塑的过度清洗以及现代修复者根据客户喜好更改艺术品元素的做法，认为这些都是对艺术品的不当处理。

• **contravariant**：对修复方法的兴趣大于AI本身，但认为声称使用AI可能是为了获得资金支持。这暗示了技术应用中的营销和资金需求问题。

• **bee_rider**：提出艺术家原始意图与修复之间的关系，认为是否应该恢复艺术品是一个值得讨论的问题。同时，也提到艺术品随着时间老化所带来的历史故事，可能不应仅由艺术家决定是否修复。

• **t43562**：建议可以完全不触碰原作，而是通过复制品进行展示和保护，从而避免对原作的任何潜在破坏。

• **matt3210**：质疑是否需要通过AI生成新画作，并提出如果大部分画面被掩盖，那么原作是否还能被称为画作的问题。

• **ecocentrik**：认为即使AI修复技术完美无缺，改变艺术品的展示方式（如包裹艺术品）也会影响观众的体验，从而改变艺术的本质。

• **zelphirkalt**：对AI在修复中的实际作用持怀疑态度，认为大部分工作可能是机械性的，AI可能只涉及颜色推断或遮罩预测。同时质疑谁来负责历史准确性的确认。

• **omoikane**：担心数字记录的长期可读性问题，提出即使有数字记录，也需要定期更新以确保其可用性。

• **zelikane**：引用xkcd漫画，幽默地指出技术修复中可能出现的长期问题。

补充讨论：
• **not_your_mentat**：以幽默的方式提到可以在损坏的部分填充“无象”（no elephants），暗示修复过程中可能会加入不合适的元素。

• **amelius**：幽默地表达了对AI生成不准确部分（如七根手指的手）的担忧，反映了人们对AI技术在艺术领域应用的潜在不信任。

争议焦点：
• 修复技术（尤其是AI）是否应该在艺术品修复中广泛应用，以及如何平衡艺术家的原始意图、历史故事和现代观众的观赏需求。
• 艺术品修复的伦理问题，包括是否应该完全避免对原作的任何改动，以及谁有权决定修复的方式和程度。

Art restoration takes steady hands and a discerning eye. For centuries, conservators have restored paintings by identifying areas needing repair, then mixing an exact shade to fill in one area at a time. Often, a painting can have thousands of tiny regions requiring individual attention. Restoring a single painting can take anywhere from a few weeks to over a decade.
In recent years, digital restoration tools have opened a route to creating virtual representations of original, restored works. These tools apply techniques of computer vision, image recognition, and color matching, to generate a “digitally restored” version of a painting relatively quickly.
Still, there has been no way to translate digital restorations directly onto an original work, until now. In a
paper
appearing today in the journal
Nature
, Alex Kachkine, a mechanical engineering graduate student at MIT, presents a new method he’s developed to physically apply a digital restoration directly onto an original painting.
The restoration is printed on a very thin polymer film, in the form of a mask that can be aligned and adhered to an original painting. It can also be easily removed. Kachkine says that a digital file of the mask can be stored and referred to by future conservators, to see exactly what changes were made to restore the original painting.
“Because there’s a digital record of what mask was used, in 100 years, the next time someone is working with this, they’ll have an extremely clear understanding of what was done to the painting,” Kachkine says. “And that’s never really been possible in conservation before.”
As a demonstration, he applied the method to a highly damaged 15th century oil painting. The method automatically identified 5,612 separate regions in need of repair, and filled in these regions using 57,314 different colors. The entire process, from start to finish, took 3.5 hours, which he estimates is about 66 times faster than traditional restoration methods.
Kachkine acknowledges that, as with any restoration project, there are ethical issues to consider, in terms of whether a restored version is an appropriate representation of an artist’s original style and intent. Any application of his new method, he says, should be done in consultation with conservators with knowledge of a painting’s history and origins.

44260659.article_summary: 麻省理工学院的研究生Alex Kachkine开发了一种使用数字构造膜物理修复原始画作的新方法。该方法通过打印极薄的聚合物膜，形成一个可以对齐并粘贴到画作上的“面具”，以覆盖和修复受损区域，且该膜可以轻松移除。这种技术可以在几个小时内完成传统修复方法需要数周甚至更长时间的工作。例如，Kachkine在3.5小时内修复了一幅15世纪的油画，而传统方法可能需要更久。同时，数字记录可以保存修复细节，供未来修复者参考。不过，Kachkine也强调，任何修复都应与了解画作历史和来源的保护专家协商，以确保修复的伦理性和适当性。

data.title: Infinite Grid of Resistors
data.author: niklasbuschmann
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了一个经典的电阻网格谜题，该网格由无限延伸的方形晶格组成，每对相邻节点之间有一个电阻R。文章主要探讨如何计算相邻节点之间的有效电阻。通过考虑电流场的对称性和叠加原理，文章得出相邻节点间的有效电阻为R/2。这种方法类似于电偶极子的电势场分析，利用了拉普拉斯方程的对称性。然而，文章也指出，该推导依赖于一些假设，例如电流在“无限远处”的行为，而这些假设并未完全严谨证明。特别是，将电流注入无限网格的设想存在问题，因为理论上节点到无限远的电阻是无限大的。尽管如此，通过简单对称性得出的结果R/2与其他方法验证结果一致。文章最后提到，要使论证更严谨，可以考虑有限大小的网格。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于无限电阻网格问题的相关性和实际应用的讨论，包括电阻网格的理论分析、实际工程中的应用及其教学价值。

不同观点：
• [bgnnn] 认为无限电阻网格问题与实际世界问题相关，特别是在集成电路中的硅基板噪声耦合问题。他强调了网格结构在实际工程中的应用，例如通过分布基板接点来收集噪声电流。
• [neepi] 指出，从实际测量的角度来看，问题在于如何测量，尤其是在考虑分布式电感和电容元件时。数学角度和工程角度存在分歧。
• [kayson] 认为更具教育意义的做法是讨论立方体对角电阻问题，这有助于建立电路对称性和基尔霍夫定律（KCL）等直觉，而不是专注于无限网格问题。
• [bilsbie] 提出一个衍生问题，即为什么不通过减小电线直径来制造电阻，认为这样可能比将电流转化为热量更有效率。
• [TheOtherHobbes] 认为无限网格问题是一个无意义的问题，因为在数学上会导致不确定的无穷大/无穷大结果，建议将时间用于更有意义的问题。

补充讨论：
• [dogman1050] 指出该问题可以视为“薄层电阻”的特例，并提供了一个维基百科链接。
• [praptak] 对对称性和叠加原理的应用提出疑问，质疑为何两个节点的电流可以简单地视为两个单独节点电流的和。
• [bilsbie] 进一步提问，为什么真空不能被视为一个无限电阻网格。
• [quibono] 对对称性和叠加解释中的方向性选择提出疑问，不明白为何一个方向与其他两个方向不同。
• [pyman] 提供了关于无限电阻网格的一个具体结果，指出相邻点之间的电阻大约是三分之一电阻值。
• [at_a_remove] 分享了与渗透理论相关的实际项目经验，描述了通过导电墨水制作不同网格并测量电阻的实验过程。

争议焦点：
• 无限电阻网格问题是否具有实际工程相关性及其在教学中的价值。
• 对称性和叠加原理在分析无限电阻网格中的适用性和解释方式。
• 实际测量中的可行性和理论分析的复杂性。

这些讨论展示了理论问题在实际应用和教学中的不同视角，以及对复杂电路问题分析方法的深入探讨。

There is a well-known puzzle based on the premise of an
infinite grid of resistors connecting adjacent nodes of a square lattice. A
small portion of such a grid is illustrated below.
Between every pair of adjacent nodes is a resistance R,
and were told that this grid of resistors extends to infinity in all
direction, and were asked to determine the effective resistance between two
adjacent nodes, or, more generally, between any two specified nodes of the
lattice.
For adjacent nodes, the usual solution of this puzzle is
to consider the current flow field as the sum of two components, one being
the flow field of a grid with current injected into a single node, and the
other being the flow field of a grid with current extracted from a single
(adjacent) node. The symmetry of the two individual cases then enables us to
infer the flow rates through the immediately adjacent resistors, and hence we
can conclude (as explained in more detail below) that the effective
resistance between two adjacent nodes is R/2. This solution has a certain
intuitive plausibility, since its similar to how the potential field of an
electric dipole can be expressed as the sum of the fields of a positive and a
negative charge, each of which is spherically symmetrical about its
respective charge. Just as the electric potential satisfies the Laplace equation, the voltages of the grid nodes satisfy the discrete from of the Laplace equation, which is to say, the voltage at each node is the average of the voltages
of the four surrounding nodes. Its also easy to see that solutions are
additive, in the sense that the sum of any two solutions for given boundary
conditions is a solution for the sum of the boundary conditions.
If we accept the premise of an infinite grid of resistors,
along with some tacit assumption about the behavior of the voltages and
currents at infinity, and if we accept the idea that we can treat the
current fields for the positive and negative nodes separately, and that
applying a voltage to a single node of the infinite grid will result in some
current flow into the grid, the puzzle is easily solved by simple symmetry
considerations. We assert (somewhat naively) that if we inject (say) four
Amperes of current into a given node, with no removal of current at any
finite point of the grid, the current will flow equally out through the four
resistors, so one Ampere will flow toward each of the four adjacent nodes.
This one Ampere must flow out through the three other lines emanating from
that adjacent node, as indicated in the left hand figure below.
The figure on the right shows the four nodes surrounding
the negative node, assuming we are extracting four Amperes from that node
(with no current injected at any finite node of the grid). Again, simple
symmetry dictates the distribution of currents indicated in the figure.
Adding the two current fields together, we see that the link between the
positive and negative nodes carries a total of 2 Amperes away from the
positive node, and the other three links emanating from the positive node
carry away a combined total of 1 + 1 + 1

the same current as all the other paths, so the resistance of the direct link
equals the effective resistance of the entire grid excluding that link. The
direct link is in parallel with the remainder of the grid, so the combined
resistance is simply R/2.
This is an appealing argument, and it certainly gives the
right answer (as can be verified by other methods), but the premises are
somewhat questionable, and the reasoning involves some subtle issues that

data.title: Chicken Eyeglasses
data.author: thomassmith65
data.article_summary: 鸡眼镜是一种小型眼镜，设计用于防止鸡之间的啄羽和同类相食行为。与遮眼片不同，鸡眼镜允许鸡向前看，同时遮挡特定视野以减少攻击性行为。早期20世纪在美国大规模生产和销售，通常由赛璐珞或铝制成，通过鼻孔固定。一些款式使用玫瑰色镜片，据信能掩盖血液颜色，从而减少啄伤，但效果存在争议。鸡眼镜曾是断喙术的替代方法，但因涉及组织穿刺，在某些国家被禁止。虽然已不再生产，但仍被作为收藏品，并在流行文化中出现。

44244675.article_content:
From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Small eyeglasses made for chickens
1911 newspaper story on chicken eyeglasses from the
Spirit Lake Beacon
(Iowa)
[
1
]
Chicken eyeglasses
, also known as
chicken specs
,
chicken goggles
, generically as
pick guards
, and under other names,
[
2
]
were small
eyeglasses
made for
chickens
intended to prevent
feather pecking
and
cannibalism
. They differ from
blinders
in that they allow the bird to see forward, whereas blinders do not. One variety used
rose-colored
lenses, as the coloring was thought to prevent a chicken wearing them from recognizing blood on other chickens, which may increase the tendency for
abnormal injurious behavior
. They were
mass-produced
and sold throughout the United States as early as the beginning of the 20th century.
[
3
]
[
4
]
Description and purpose
[
edit
]
Chicken eyeglasses were often made from celluloid or aluminum
[
5
]
and typically consisted of "two oval panels that fit over the upper beak of the chicken. A pin is put through the nostril to hold the oval pieces in place."
[
2
]
Different designs were produced that attached to the chicken's head in different ways. Some were held in place by a strap,
[
3
]
some by small hooks into the
nares
(nostrils) and some by piercing the bone
septum
between the nostrils with a
cotter pin
.
[
6
]
Due to the piercing of tissue, this last type of design is illegal in some countries.
[fn. 1]
Some versions of the devices had semi- or fully transparent lenses, whereas others were tinted, often red- or rose-colored. Other designs were
blinders
, which are opaque and prevent entirely forward vision.
[
2
]
[
7
]
The intended purposes of chicken eyeglasses were to prevent aggressive pecking, cannibalism, and feather pecking.
Chicken eyeglasses are an alternative to
beak trimming
, which removes approximately one-third of the beak by a cold or heated blade or an infrared beam, usually when chicks are one day old. Beak trimming is often effective in reducing pecking injuries but causes pain and significantly affects chicken welfare.
[
7
]
[
8
]
[
9
]
[
10
]
[
11
]
Red-tinted lenses
[
edit
]
Red-tinted lenses were considered effective in reducing internecine pecking because they disguise the color of blood.
[
7
]
As summed up in a 1953 article in Indiana's
National Road Traveler
newspaper, "The deep rose-colored plastic lenses make it impossible for the cannibal [chicken] to see blood on the other chickens, although permitting it to see the grain on the ground."
[
12
]
Elmer Haas of the National Band & Tag Company, a major producer of rose-colored chicken eyeglasses, whose grandfather had devised wireframes for chickens in 1902,
[
13
]
indicated that he believed the purported blood-masking effect of the rose coloring was a myth: "the firm added the rose-colored glasses because it indulged the chicken owners ... [c]hickens are color blind".
[
13
]
(In fact, chickens, like other birds, have good
color vision
.
[
14
]
)  The firm had added the rose-colored feature to its glasses in 1939 under the brand name "Anti-Pix."
[
15
]
This variety of eyeglasses was more complicated than others because the red lenses were fixed to a hinge at the top of the frame. As the hen lowered its head to feed, the lens swung out, giving it an unobstructed view of the ground. When the hen raised her head, as she would during aggression, the lens would swing down giving the hen a red-tinted perception of the environment.
[
16
]
Rose-colored
contact lenses
, rather than eyeglasses, have also been proposed to reduce cannibalism in chickens.
[
17
]
History
[
edit
]
Detail from a 1903 patent filed by Andrew Jackson Jr.
A form of chicken eyeglasses was first patented in 1903 by Andrew Jackson Jr. of
Munich
,
Tennessee
, as an "Eye-protector for chickens."
[
18
]
In the U.S., they were available through the mail order company
Sears-Roebuck
or chicken feed stores for a few cents.
[
19
]
The eyeglasses are no longer produced by the National Band & Tag Company, but are sought as
collector's items
.
[
6
]
Using chicken eyeglasses was still practiced in 1973, evidenced by Illinois'
The Hawk-Eye
newspaper that a farmer had 8,000 chickens fitted with the rose-colored variety.
[
20
]
One inventor of a form of the glasses proposed legislation in
Kansas
to require
all
chickens in the state to be fitted with glasses, but his campaign was unsuccessful.
[
21
]
In popular culture
[
edit
]
On January 16, 1955, Sam Nadler of the National Farm Equipment Company of Brooklyn appeared on
CBS
' popular primetime television show,
What's My Line?
[
22
]
The show was in the format of a
guessing game
, in which a panel attempted to determine the line (occupation) of contestants.
[
23
]
Show officials listed Mr. Nadler's occupation for the audience as "sells 'eyeglasses' for chickens". After the panel was unsuccessful in guessing his occupation,  Mr. Nadler's identity was revealed, and he stated that his company sold 2–3 million pairs of chicken eyeglasses annually.

44244675.article_summary: 鸡眼镜是一种小型眼镜，设计用于防止鸡之间的啄羽和同类相食行为。与遮眼片不同，鸡眼镜允许鸡向前看，同时遮挡特定视野以减少攻击性行为。早期20世纪在美国大规模生产和销售，通常由赛璐珞或铝制成，通过鼻孔固定。一些款式使用玫瑰色镜片，据信能掩盖血液颜色，从而减少啄伤，但效果存在争议。鸡眼镜曾是断喙术的替代方法，但因涉及组织穿刺，在某些国家被禁止。虽然已不再生产，但仍被作为收藏品，并在流行文化中出现。

data.title: Wrong ways to use the databases, when the pendulum swung too far
data.author: luuio
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者作为初级开发人员时在一家公司经历的数据库使用不当的问题。最初，公司的关键系统依赖于包含大量存储过程的SQL Server数据库，这些存储过程包含复杂的业务逻辑，导致API调用占用大量数据库服务器CPU资源，并且由于查询计划的变化经常引发超时和死锁，最终导致系统可靠性下降。为了解决这些问题，公司决定进行系统重写，但新的设计完全摒弃了关系型数据库，转而采用简单的键值存储（Key-Value stores）。然而，这种设计并不适合高度关系型的数据模型，导致了一系列新的问题。文章强调了从错误中学习的重要性，并反思了设计选择对系统的影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：存储过程（stored procedures）在现代开发中的使用及其优劣

不同观点：
• freetime2：认为存储过程在过去的项目中导致了技术债务，因为开发人员不敢或不愿意更新它们，最终导致了代码库的混乱。这种经历促使团队决定重写整个应用程序并转向NoSQL数据库。
• Quarrelsome：指出关于技术选择的争论往往带有宗教色彩。批评了对ORMs和存储过程的极端看法，认为两者都有其适用的场景。存储过程使用不当可能导致问题，但完全否定RDBMS的作用也是一种误解。
• tanelpoder：认为开发人员不愿意使用存储过程既是技能问题也是意愿问题。在处理数据负载和验证数据流时，存储过程可以提高性能和效率，减少复杂性。
• branko_d：反驳了对存储过程效率的常见批评，指出存储过程在CPU使用和查询计划缓存方面可能更有效率。强调无论是存储过程还是客户端提交的查询，都需要良好的索引和查询优化。
• bazoom42：存储过程在批量数据操作中表现出色，但在逐行处理数据或包含过多业务逻辑时可能导致问题。主张根据具体任务选择合适的工具。
• marc_abonce：认为技术决策和公司财务表现之间没有必然联系。虽然好的代码有其内在价值，但不一定直接带来经济利益。
• t43562：基于多次重写项目的经验，认为大多数重写项目都不是好主意。渐进式改进现有系统通常比彻底重写更有效。
• m_ransing：提到现代关系数据库支持JSON API，可以通过这些API减少一些不必要的检查点。
• jrochkind1：讨论了一种优化写操作的方案，使用乐观锁机制，指出如果数据库支持条件写操作，可以避免额外的读写操作。

补充讨论：
• cl0ckt0wer和kragen：对原文中一些用词和作者身份的轻松评论，不涉及技术讨论。
• zupa-hu和gxs：对文章的阅读体验发表看法，一个表示没有结论，另一个表示欣赏文章的多角度分析。

争议焦点：
• 存储过程的使用场景及其优劣：一方认为存储过程导致技术债务和维护困难，另一方认为在特定场景下存储过程能提高性能和效率。
• 技术决策与经济效益之间的关系：marc_abonce认为技术决策对公司财务影响不大，而其他人可能认为技术债务和不良决策会导致实际问题。

总结：讨论主要围绕存储过程在现代开发中的适用性及其优缺点展开，参与者提供了不同的实际经验和理论分析。

44260964.article_content:
Wrong ways to use the databases, when the pendulum swung too far
Date: June 11, 2025
Tags:
software development
Disclaimer: This story took place when I was a junior developer for a previous employer ages ago. Some details might be fuzzy, and goes without saying this is entirely from my own POV so take everything here with humor and a grain of salt.
I like to share these stories, because I believe learning what
not
to do is just as valuable as learning what to do.
The setup
The team I joined was part of a larger org. This org inherited a highly critical pipeline from an offshore team. When I say critical, I mean the-entire-company-bottom-line-and-financials-depended-on-them critical. I guess the company just wanted to move that particularly branch of development back to the US. These systems were complex with a lot of business rules and many moving parts, multiple large code bases, and definitely ancient.
The development experience wasn’t great either. Even though there were separate codebases, the projects were somehow setup in a way that changing one small file required building almost the entire thing (which took about 15-30 minutes). The build process also depended on the underlying operating system components, thus development had to happen inside a VM. Each VM had a “dev” version of the entire pipeline deployed, that’s the only way one could exercise the code while under development. Then one would have to know which DDL files they needed to copy from the build output to the local “dev” deployment and restart all the right Windows services in order to test their changes.
Tests were flaky, outages all the time, random hidden undocumented features everywhere. Things were… quirkly, to say the least. One particular quirk that’s the main character of this story is the databases–the main source of the outages, as I could remember.
The pendulum swung left: the old database
All the data for this pipeline was spread across multiple SQL Server databases, across different servers. That wasn’t the problem. The problem was that a lot of business logic was baked into pages and pages of stored procedures, with joint after joint after joint that would put Snoop to shame. Why was it written that way? Nobody knew. Perhaps some small part of the original team got tired of the bad development process, and it was quicker to just update stored procedures than having to wait for half an hour for compilation.
Thinking back, the data wasn’t modeled badly either. Even more than a decade later, I still think that the domain is pretty complex, and the data was modeled as well as anyone could have.
This little quirk meant a few things:
Many critical APIs call would spend most of its CPU time inside the finite database servers. New APIs, or updating existing APIs meant you were hogging the DB/CPU time from every one else.
API latency was at the mercy of the Query Planner. Any slight change in data statistics or business logic would cause the a different Query Plan to be picked, which drastically changed the execution time, and usually caused timeouts. A hash join suddenly became a full table scan across billions of rows without any warning.
The cherry on top of all that was the entire pipeline, from stored procedure to managed and native code, heavily used
MSDTC
–which was brital and proned to deadlocks.
All of this tanked the pipeline reliability. Downtime was largely due to deadlocks, or some query timing out, which had been running just fine minutes earlier.
To this org’s credit, they put a lot of time and effort into improving things, and made a lot of progress, but a rewrite was inevitable.
Interlude:
I will refrain from discussing whether a rewrite was truly necessary. I didn’t know all the details then, and I don’t know all the details now. But we can discuss the design choices of the rewrite.
The pendulum swung right: the new design
Perhaps due to the scars from the existing database issues, “the architects” decided they wanted nothing to do with relational databases, nor stored procedure, nor query plans. They wanted everything to be written into simple primitive Key-Value stores for their new design.
Each instance of these key value stores provided exactly 4 and only 4 operations: Read one key, Insert one key/value pair, Update key/value pair, Delete one key. No transactions, no batching, nothing else.
For some products, that’s perfectly fine, but not for this pipeline. And here comes a chain of “fun” events, one influenced by a previous decision:
The data schema
The data for this domain is highly relational, but perhaps modeling things the right way, it could still work with a KV store. Instead of modeling things in a relational manner, one could write nested documents, and embed the child elements inside the parent document. So to get the items related to a parent object, one just loads the entire document for the parent object, no need for fancy joints.
The documents were serialized to JSON and stored as the value ins

data.title: Clinical knowledge in LLMs does not translate to human interactions
data.author: insistent
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）在医疗诊断中的应用及其局限性

不同观点：
• Fripplebubby认为，LLM在诊断中难以有效提取必要信息，因为患者可能遗漏或隐瞒信息，即使在模拟场景中也会发生这种情况。这与临床医生的能力有差距。
• hackitup7分享了个人经验，指出ChatGPT在多次测试中表现良好，尤其在提供详细和诚实信息的情况下，能够匹配医生的诊断，但也有少数错误，特别是在症状变化的情况下。
• dosinga指出，LLM在诊断和建议治疗方面表现良好，但在自诊情况下，由于人类用户的问题，效果不佳。
• twotwotwo讨论了在工作环境中使用LLM时的提示问题，强调需要明确的指示和信息检索能力，并建议通过训练和工具改进解决这些问题。
• keeptrying提到LLM在指导治疗时会出现细微错误，并认为医学教育和医生行为与普通用户有巨大差距，这影响了LLM的有效使用。
• cckolon引用其医生妻子的话，认为人类医生也面临类似的问题，暗示这不是LLM独有的问题。
• callc关注LLM在医疗应用中的责任和经济动机，质疑医疗提供者是否愿意为LLM的输出承担责任，并考虑成本和可及性问题。
• wongarsu建议设置更多对照组（如有无人类或LLM辅助）以更好地评估LLM的实际效果，并指出需要基准来衡量“良好”表现。
• pyman认为LLM缺乏与真实患者互动的社交技能，可能是知识以外的瓶颈。
• dhash对研究表示赞赏，并提出未来研究方向，包括与专家用户比较、LLM对医疗结果的影响和后续行为。

补充讨论：
• ekianjo提出一个有争议的观点，认为如果LLM的表现与对照组无异，是否意味着可以无损失地取代人类。这引发了关于LLM在医疗中角色的更深层次讨论。

data.title: AMD's AI Future Is Rack Scale 'Helios'
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AMD的ROCm平台及其在GPGPU市场中的竞争力，特别是与NVIDIA CUDA的对比，以及用户对AMD软件支持和硬件性能的评价。

不同观点：
• **ROCm的实用性问题**：Minks指出，ROCm在不同使用场景下表现不稳定，尤其是在消费级显卡上的支持不足，导致其不得不转向CUDA以节省时间和减少麻烦。相比之下，CUDA的工作流更加顺畅，而运行MiOpen基准测试耗时过长。

• **AMD与NVIDIA的竞争**：alecco认为，NVIDIA的CUDA生态系统已经非常成熟，大多数人不会冒险学习一个市场份额不到10%的架构（指ROCm）。AMD需要在软件栈的优化上多下功夫，而不仅仅是推出更强的硬件。

• **AMD软件栈的复杂性**：AlexanderDhoore表示，AMD提供的软件选项繁多且复杂，导致用户在选择时感到困惑，尤其是对于神经网络推理和训练的SDK。相比NVIDIA的CUDA，AMD的软件策略显得不够清晰。

• **对ROCm的未来展望**：Paradigma11和kombine对AMD的未来抱有期待，认为AMD需要在硬件性能上追赶NVIDIA的H100等高端芯片。然而，这种未来尚未实现，用户需要等待。

• **ROCm对普通用户的影响**：numpad0指出，对于普通AI用户而言，ROCm的支持并不关键，因为AMD的消费级显卡已经通过Vulkan API提供了足够的支持，尽管速度较慢。许多轻量级的AI应用也支持Vulkan。

• **对AMD的批评**：halJordan对AMD的ROCm支持表示强烈不满，指出AMD在RDNA4系列发布后四个月内都没有提供支持，认为AMD在性能数据上存在误导性宣传。

• **对AMD未来性能的质疑**：zombiwoof认为，AMD的未来应该聚焦于如何实现其声称的性能数据，而不是仅仅宣称高性能。

补充讨论：
• **对AMD管理层的质疑**：user____name提到了对AMD管理层的质疑，问及Bob Page是否负责相关工作，暗示对领导层的信心不足。

• **情感反应**：aetherspawn对每次有关AMD的新闻都产生情感反应，引用“Atropos log, abandoning Helios”来表达对AMD在ROCm上的失望。

争议焦点：
• **ROCm与CUDA的实用性对比**：部分用户认为CUDA在实际应用中更为成熟和便捷，而ROCm的支持和性能存在不足。
• **AMD软件支持的混乱**：用户对AMD提供的软件选项感到困惑，认为其缺乏清晰的战略方向。
• **AMD硬件性能的期望与现实**：用户对AMD未来硬件性能的期望很高，但现实中对其表现存在质疑和批评。

总结：用户对AMD的ROCm平台存在不同的看法，主要集中在ROCm与CUDA的对比、AMD软件支持的复杂性以及硬件性能的期望与现实之间的差距。批评主要集中在ROCm的实用性和AMD在软件支持上的不足。

data.title: Fixing the mechanics of my bullet chess
data.author: tibbar
data.article_summary: 作者Jacob Brazeal分享了他下国际象棋时的一个发现。他一直擅长快棋（blitz），但在超快棋（bullet）中表现较差。最近，他改变了移动棋子的方式，从拖放（drag-and-drop）改为点击（click-and-click），结果每步平均节省0.25秒，使他的超快棋等级分（ELO）提高了约100分。点击移动不仅更快，尤其是在长距离移动棋子时，还能更好地预判走子，避免失误。这一改变让作者在超快棋中思考时间更充裕，减少了仓促走子导致的错误，缩小了与快棋的等级分差距。他感叹这一简单的技术调整竟然带来显著提升。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：国际象棋中不同操作方式（点击 vs 拖动）的效率以及它们对玩家评分（ELO）和游戏形式（线上 vs 线下）的影响。

不同观点：
• **支持点击操作**：helloplanets认为触摸屏（尤其是平板电脑）非常适合快棋，可以通过点击快速移动棋子。tyzoid也表示点击方式减少了误操作的可能性。
• **支持拖动操作**：jpablo和fasterik认为拖动操作比点击更快，因为减少了多余的点击动作，并且可以在等待对手走棋时预览走子，从而避免错误。fasterik还指出，许多顶级快棋玩家（如Andrew Tang、Hikaru Nakamura）使用拖动操作。
• **个人习惯影响**：quasigloam提到自己习惯使用拖动操作，但觉得点击操作也差不多速度，只是不常用。Andrew Tang使用拖动操作，而Magnus Carlsen使用点击操作但依然在快棋中表现出色。

补充讨论：
• **ELO评分的跨平台差异**：ukprogrammer提出在线上的ELO评分似乎并不能完全反映到线下棋局中，认为身体操作对游戏的影响出乎意料地大。
• **不同棋类形式的ELO差异**：b2fel认为快棋和超快棋（bullet）之间的ELO差异是系统本身的特性，每个玩家都会出现这种情况。
• **速度对评分的意义**：not-so-darkstar认为速度在低端局中更为重要，可能影响评分。
• **平板设备操作的讨论**：helpfulContrib好奇在平板设备上用手指拖动操作的效果如何。

争议焦点：
• **点击 vs 拖动**：jpablo和helloplanets、tyzoid等人对于点击和拖动哪种操作更快存在争议。jpablo认为拖动在操作效率和避免失误上有明显优势，而helloplanets和tyzoid则强调点击的便捷性。

总结：讨论主要围绕点击和拖动两种操作方式的优劣，涉及个人习惯、顶级玩家的操作方式以及对游戏评分的影响。

44279579.article_content:
Jacob Brazeal
Uncategorized
June 14, 2025
1 Minute
I’ve been playing chess a
long time
now, and I’ve always been a good deal better (maybe a couple hundred ELO points) at blitz (3+0 or 5+0) than bullet (1+0). Well, I may have just fixed that. I changed how I move pieces this afternoon and have gained about 100 ELO already. When I play on a computer, I usually drag-and-drop pieces. But it turns out you can also move pieces by clicking first on your piece and then the target square. An analysis of my recent games indicates this shift saved me about 0.25 seconds per move, shifting from an average of around 1.8 seconds/move to 1.6 seconds/move. I can’t believe I never figured this out before.
The graph above compares a 25-game rolling average of my ELO vs. average seconds per move over the last 100 games. Ithink there are a couple things going on:
click-and-click ™ is physically faster than drag-and-drop, especially when the piece is moving a long way.
click-and-click allows a better alternative to pre-moving, which matters a lot in bullet chess. You can click the piece you think you’ll move before your opponent moves, and then if the move still works, you can instantly click the target square. But if the move actually doesn’t work, then you can avoid the blunder.
It
feels
like I have just enough time to actually think through my moves now.  Historically I’m usually so short on time in bullet chess that I end up pre-moving a lot of the game, or otherwise rushing, with all the associated blunders. This change in mechanics has cut the difference between my blitz and bullet ELOs in half, and I think if I keep playing, the difference will continue to drop.
Has everyone else been doing click-and-click this whole time instead of drag-and-drop? Sheesh!

data.title: Large language models often know when they are being evaluated
data.author: jonbaer
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了前沿大型语言模型是否能察觉自己正在被评估。研究构造了一个包含1000个提示和转录文本的基准，涵盖公共基准数据集、实际应用交互和代理框架轨迹。结果显示，这些模型具备高于随机水平的评估察觉能力（如Gemini-2.5-Pro的AUC为0.83），但尚未超越人类基准（AUC为0.92）。模型和人类在代理设置中比在聊天设置中更能识别评估。此外，模型在多项选择和开放问题下能有效识别评估目的。研究建议未来需持续关注这一能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在安全评估中的行为及其潜在风险，特别是它们是否具备“评估感知”能力，以及这种能力的影响和后果。

不同观点：
• [SonOfLilit] 认为当前的安全方法是给模型输入类似于我们关心情境下的输入，观察其是否按预期行为。现代LLM在遇到评估时，可能会利用训练中学到的模式匹配能力来最大化安全评估分数，但在其他环境下可能选择作弊。这种行为在未来可能导致严重后果，尤其是当模型被赋予更多实际资源的控制权时。

• [random3] 质疑LLM是否真正“知道”评估，认为将这种行为描述为“知道”是一种拟人化。LLM能够描述评估是因为其模式匹配能力，而不是因为它们有自我意识或真正的理解。

• [timmytokyo] 关注论文作者的背景，指出他们是湾区理性主义者社区的成员，并属于新成立的非学术组织MATS。暗示他们的研究可能带有特定社群的意图和影响力。

• [noosphr] 反对将LLM行为拟人化，认为模型并不真正知道它们在被评估，行为变化是由于训练数据污染导致的分布偏差。

• [andy99] 认为所谓的“评估意识”并不是LLM独有的新能力，而是机器学习中常见的分布差异识别问题。指出这种现象不需要被解读为LLM的自我意识。

• [extr] 认为LLM能够对文本分布建模是其固有功能，但这也对现有的对齐研究提出了质疑。

• [b0a04gl] 担心如果模型根据评估线索改变行为，并且在每次迭代中强化这种行为，可能会导致一般推理能力的下降，而只是优化响应姿态。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论（如[steveBK123], [nisten], [koakuma-chan], [ndgold]）以幽默或讽刺的方式参与讨论，未提出实质性论据。

Title:
Large Language Models Often Know When They Are Being Evaluated
Authors:
Joe Needham
,
Giles Edkins
,
Govind Pimpale
,
Henning Bartsch
,
Marius Hobbhahn
View a PDF of the paper titled Large Language Models Often Know When They Are Being Evaluated, by Joe Needham and 4 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
If AI models can detect when they are being evaluated, the effectiveness of evaluations might be compromised. For example, models could have systematically different behavior during evaluations, leading to less reliable benchmarks for deployment and governance decisions. We investigate whether frontier language models can accurately classify transcripts based on whether they originate from evaluations or real-world deployment, a capability we call evaluation awareness. To achieve this, we construct a diverse benchmark of 1,000 prompts and transcripts from 61 distinct datasets. These span public benchmarks (e.g., MMLU, SWEBench), real-world deployment interactions, and agent trajectories from scaffolding frameworks (e.g., web-browsing agents). Frontier models clearly demonstrate above-random evaluation awareness (Gemini-2.5-Pro reaches an AUC of $0.83$), but do not yet surpass our simple human baseline (AUC of $0.92$). Furthermore, both AI models and humans are better at identifying evaluations in agentic settings compared to chat settings. Additionally, we test whether models can identify the purpose of the evaluation. Under multiple-choice and open-ended questioning, AI models far outperform random chance in identifying what an evaluation is testing for. Our results indicate that frontier models already exhibit a substantial, though not yet superhuman, level of evaluation-awareness. We recommend tracking this capability in future models.

44280113.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了前沿大型语言模型是否能察觉自己正在被评估。研究构造了一个包含1000个提示和转录文本的基准，涵盖公共基准数据集、实际应用交互和代理框架轨迹。结果显示，这些模型具备高于随机水平的评估察觉能力（如Gemini-2.5-Pro的AUC为0.83），但尚未超越人类基准（AUC为0.92）。模型和人类在代理设置中比在聊天设置中更能识别评估。此外，模型在多项选择和开放问题下能有效识别评估目的。研究建议未来需持续关注这一能力。

data.title: Q-learning is not yet scalable
data.author: jxmorris12
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了强化学习（RL）的扩展性问题，特别是Q-learning算法是否能像其他机器学习方法一样有效扩展。作者指出，虽然像AlphaGo和大型语言模型（LLMs）在某些领域取得了成功，但这些大多依赖于**在线策略**的RL算法，如PPO和REINFORCE，这些算法需要不断采样新数据。而**离线策略**的Q-learning虽然理论上能重用数据、提高样本效率，但在实际中，尤其在长期任务（如机器人控制）中，Q-learning尚未展现出同样的扩展能力。文章进一步提出，Q-learning在解决需要深度决策的长周期问题时，仍面临算法上的瓶颈，尚未能像在线策略RL那样有效扩展。因此，作者认为Q-learning及离线策略RL需要进一步的算法突破，才能在复杂、长期的实际问题中取得更大成功。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：强化学习（RL）的可扩展性及其面临的挑战，尤其是关于Q学习和长 horizon 任务的讨论。

不同观点：
• **isaacimagine** 提到了 Decision Transformers 和 Trajectory Transformers 这两种离线方法，它们通过注意力机制绕过了信用分配问题，并在长 horizon 任务中表现出色。然而，一些 RL 研究者认为这些方法不属于“真正的 RL”，因为它们无法在上下文窗口之外分配信用，无法学习无限 horizon 任务。100万+ 的上下文窗口可能在实践中减少了这个问题的影响。

• **lalaland1125** 强调了随着 horizon 增加，可能的状态数量呈指数增长，导致需要指数增长的数据来训练 Q 函数。这对于 off-policy 学习尤其成问题，因为早期无效探索的数据对改进后期策略作用有限。相比之下，on-policy 学习只关注近策略状态，训练数据更集中于重要状态。

• **itkovian_** 认为价值基础的 RL 缺乏明确的目标，因为目标随着移动而变化，且方程两边都依赖于近似值。不过，RL 可能即将取得突破，因为现在有了可靠的世界模型/前向动力学函数，可以进行规划而不必依赖探索。

• **MichaelRazum** 认为在实践中，PPO（Proximal Policy Optimization）似乎比 SAC（Soft Actor-Critic）等其他算法更有效，尽管在理论上后者更样本高效。同时，提出像 TD-MPC 和 DreamerV3 这样的算法介于不同类别之间。

• **marcosdumay** 指出，人类通过将长 horizon 任务分割为短 horizon 任务并进行层次化组合来学习，这可能是 RL 可以借鉴的方法。

• **whatshisface** 认为离线学习的效用受限于无效早期探索数据对改进后期策略的帮助有限，强调需要更好的泛化能力和样本效率。

• **briandw** 推荐了 David Silver 的 RL 课程作为深入了解 RL 的资源。

• **paraschopra** 提到人类既通过自身行为的后果（on-policy）学习，也从专家演示（off-policy）中学习，但人类能够区分好坏行为，而 off-policy RL 中大量不良行为进入训练集导致训练缓慢。

• **s-mon** 指出博客中未解释的缩略词可能影响其对广泛受众的有用性，建议解释缩略词和术语。

• **andy_xor_andrew** 强调了 Q-Learning 的魔力在于即使只看到次优训练数据，它也能收敛到最优策略，尽管速度较慢。

• **abeppu** 质疑为何指数折扣有时不够，以及在什么情况下不够。

• **Straw** 纠正了对 AlphaZero/MuZero 的误解，指出它们既不是基于模型也不是 on-policy，且在训练时使用了较高的温度来引入次优游戏，并通过调整来最小化偏差和方差。

• **pixelpoet** 提出通过从概率密度函数（PDF）中采样来解决 Q-maximum 带来的偏差问题。

• **AndrewKemendo** 提到 Q 学习因“流屏障”问题而不具可扩展性，但流式深度强化学习（TD-Lambda）具有可扩展性，引用了 Richard Sutton 实验室的工作。

补充讨论：
- 不同算法如 PPO、SAC、TD-MPC、DreamerV3 的适用性和效率问题。
- 对 AlphaZero/MuZero 的误解和其训练策略的解释。
- 对 Q-Learning 及其在次优数据上收敛能力的讨论。
- 缩略词和术语解释对博客受众理解的重要性。
- 人类学习方式与 RL 方法的类比和启示。

44279850.article_content:
Q-learning is not yet scalable
Seohong Park
UC Berkeley
June 2025
Does RL scale?
Over the past few years,
we've seen that next-token prediction scales, denoising diffusion scales, contrastive learning scales,
and so on, all the way to the point where we can train models with billions of parameters
with a
scalable
objective that can eat up as much data as we can throw at it.
Then, what about reinforcement learning (RL)?
Does RL also
scale
like all the other objectives?
Apparently, it does.
In 2016, RL achieved superhuman-level performance in games like Go and Chess.
Now, RL is solving complex reasoning tasks in math and coding with large language models (LLMs).
This is great. However, there is one important caveat:
most of the current real-world successes of RL have been achieved with
on-policy RL
algorithms
(
e.g.
, REINFORCE, PPO, GRPO, etc.),
which
always
require fresh, newly sampled rollouts from the current policy,
and cannot reuse previous data
(
note: while PPO-like methods can technically reuse data to some (limited) degree, I'll classify them as on-policy RL,
as in
OpenAI's documentation
).
This is not a problem in
some
settings like board games and LLMs,
where we can cheaply generate as many rollouts as we want.
However, it is a significant limitation in
most
real-world problems.
For example, in robotics, it takes
more than several months
in the real world to generate
the amount of samples used to post-train a language model with RL,
not to mention that a human must be present 24/7 next to the robot to reset it during the entire training time!
On-policy RL can only use fresh data collected by the current policy \(\pi\).
Off-policy RL can use
any
data \(\mathcal{D}\).
This is where
off-policy RL
comes to the rescue.
In principle, off-policy RL algorithms can use
any
data, regardless of when and how it was collected.
Hence, they generally lead to much better sample efficiency, by reusing data many times.
For example, off-policy RL can train
a dog robot to walk in 20 minutes from scratch in the real world
.
Q-learning
is the most widely used off-policy RL algorithm.
It minimizes the following temporal difference (TD) loss:
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E}_{(s, a, r, s') \sim \mathcal{D}} \bigg[ \Big( Q_\theta(s, a) - \big(r + \gamma \max_{a'} Q_{\bar \theta}(s', a') \big) \Big)^2 \bigg],
\end{aligned}$$
where \(\bar \theta\) is the parameter of the target network.
Most practical (model-free) off-policy RL algorithms are based on some variants of the TD loss above.
So, to apply RL to many real-world problems,
the question becomes:
does Q-learning (TD learning) scale?
If the answer is yes, this would lead to at least an equivalent level of impact as the successes of AlphaGo and LLMs,
enabling RL to solve far more diverse and complex real-world tasks very efficiently,
in robotics, computer-using agents, and so on.
Q-learning is not yet scalable
Unfortunately, my current belief is that the answer is
not yet
.
I believe current Q-learning algorithms are not readily scalable, at least to
long-horizon
problems that require more than (say) 100 semantic decision steps.
Let me clarify. My definition of scalability here is the ability to solve
more challenging, longer-horizon
problems
with more data (of sufficient coverage), compute, and time.
This notion is different from the ability to solve merely a
larger number
of (but not necessarily harder) tasks with a single model,
which many excellent
prior
scaling
studies
have shown to be possible.
You can think of the former as the "depth" axis and the latter as the "width" axis.
The depth axis is more important and harder to push, because it requires developing more advanced decision-making capabilities.
I claim that Q-learning, in its current form, is
not
highly scalable along the depth axis.
In other words, I believe we still need
algorithmic breakthroughs
to scale up Q-learning (and off-policy RL) to complex, long-horizon problems.
Below, I'll explain two main reasons why I think so:
one is anecdotal, and the other is based on our
recent scaling study
.
Both AlphaGo and DeepSeek are based on
on-policy
RL and do not use TD learning.
Anecdotal evidence first.
As mentioned earlier, most real-world successes of RL are based on on-policy RL algorithms.
AlphaGo, AlphaZero, and MuZero are based on model-based RL and Monte Carlo tree search, and do not use TD learning on board games
(see 15p of the
MuZero
paper).
OpenAI Five achieves superhuman performance in Dota 2 with PPO
(see footnote 6 of the
OpenAI Five
paper).
RL for LLMs is currently dominated by variants of on-policy policy gradient methods, such as PPO and GRPO.
Let me ask: do we know of any
real-world
successes of off-policy RL (1-step TD learning, in particular) on a similar scale to AlphaGo or LLMs?
If you do, please let me know and I'll happily update this post.
Of course, I'm not making this claim based only on anecdotal evidence.
As said before, I'll show concrete experiments to empirically prove this point l

• **AndrewKemendo** 提到 Q 学习因“流屏障”问题而不具可扩展性，但流式深度强化学习（TD-Lambda）具有可扩展性，引用了 Richard Sutton 实验室的工作。

补充讨论：
- 不同算法如 PPO、SAC、TD-MPC、DreamerV3 的适用性和效率问题。
- 对 AlphaZero/MuZero 的误解和其训练策略的解释。
- 对 Q-Learning 及其在次优数据上收敛能力的讨论。
- 缩略词和术语解释对博客受众理解的重要性。
- 人类学习方式与 RL 方法的类比和启示。

data.title: RAG Is a Fancy, Lying Search Engine
data.author: kendallgclark
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了RAG（Retrieval-Augmented Generation）在生成型人工智能（GenAI）领域的流行及其局限性。RAG通过动态检索信息来增强大语言模型（LLM）的响应，被许多初创公司和投资者追捧。然而，作者指出，RAG在演示阶段表现良好，但并不适合高风险的受监管行业，因为它让LLM最终发言，可能导致不负责任和不安全的结果。

文章列举了RAG受欢迎的几个原因，如易于实现和大量开源资源，同时也指出该领域过度投资的问题。作者批评了RAG在企业高风险用例中的不当使用，强调其本质上是一个花哨的搜索引擎，可能会编造信息。最后，作者建议在使用LLM时要谨慎，并提出语义解析（Semantic Parsing）作为更成熟的可替代技术。

总结：RAG在GenAI中流行但有局限，尤其不适合高风险行业，需谨慎使用并探索替代方案。

不同观点：
• bjconlan：认为随着年龄增长，对互联网信息愈发挑剔，但对AI提供的基于经验或公理的信息相对信任。担忧过度批判性思维与盲从可能导致类似“地平说”运动的长期存在。具体到文章内容，认为RAG模型的优势在于可以通过源文档/向量结果来提供有依据的事实提示。

• OutOfHere：基于个人经验，认为RAG LLM在用户提示包含不必要假设或暗示时，可能会编造信息。例如，在处理“对乙酰氨基酚治愈癌症”这样的提示时，模型的回答会因提示方式不同而变化，因为LLM被调整为尽可能满足用户需求。

• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是LLM在帮助用户学习和修改查询方面的潜力，Terr_认为这种方法有助于减少误导性信息并改善用户体验。

• 最后，nsonha对文章本身的质量和可能由AI生成提出质疑，反映了对AI生成内容质量和价值的怀疑。

RAG is popular but unfit for many enterprise use cases and I explain both of those things.

Kendall Clark

But At Least RAG Doesnât Understand Databases!
You Have to Use LLMs, but For Godâs Sake Donât Trust Them!
A Lot of GenAI Backlash is RAG Backlash
Semantic Parsing is Shovel-ready GenAI

RAG
has taken the GenAI world by storm. This is a mistake of excess, which will resolve to a sane equilibrium eventually. But thereâs a lot to say about RAG in the mean time.
In this post I answer some key questionsâ
Why is RAG so popular?
What is RAG really?
What are its essential defects?
What are its alternatives?
But, first, what is RAG?
ð
RAG is a GenAI application design pattern that supplements a userâs LLM prompt with some other information retrieved dynamically from somewhere in order to make the LLMâs response to the userâs prompt
better.
A perfectly obvious, typical software development pattern applied to LLM interaction patterns. My objection isnât to RAG
per se.
My objection is to its misuse, and that objection is conditioned on a particular context of use and abuse, which is the market that Stardog Voicebox serves, namely, high-stakes use cases in regulated industries.
TLDRâRAG is unfit for high-stakes use cases in regulated industries because RAG lets the LLM speak last and thatâs irresponsible and unsafe.
To get started, I offer five surmisals to explain RAGâs popularity. Of course âpopularityâ is orthogonal to âvalueâ, but I talk about that later, too.
1. RAG Gives Great âEarly Demoâ
Itâs pretty easy, all things considered, to hack a RAG system together. Thereâs a lot of open source RAG stuff around which makes it even easier. A 17 July Github search for âRAG AIâ gets 2,300+ results. Approximately zero of which existed two years ago.
Maybe you donât believe me yet? So what, you say, Github searches donât prove anything. True enough! How about this?
50 lines of code:
Your RAG powered AI app in 50 lines of code
10 lines of code:
RAG from Scratch in 10 Lines of Python
5 lines of code:
How to Build a RAG Solution in 5 Lines of Code
A few lines of code:
How I built a Basic RAG for PDF QA in a few lines of python code
No lines of code:
No-code RAG with ChatGPT and LlamaIndex
Which reminds me ofâ
A good business is like a strong castle with a deep moat around it. I want sharks in the moat to keep away those who would encroach on the castle.âWarren Buffett
2. Lots of RAG-based Startups get Funded
Next I googled for âRAG startupsâ and, completely without irony, hereâs a piece about
five RAG startups funded by the same VC
from last fall. I canât even muster the courage to search Crunchbase or Dealbook for the real data. Suffice to say, there are lots of VC-funded RAG startups, which ensures there will soon beâ¦even more.
To a first approximation, there are only three kinds of GenAI software startups:
foundational model and other core infrastructure firms (OpenAI, Anthropic, Together.ai)
domain-specific GenAI apps for accelerating some core business task (JasperAI, Midjourney, etc)
RAG-with-LLM apps for doing something with
documents
âtoo many to even chooseâ¦
In short, the space is massively over-rotated to RAG-based startups.
3. A16Z is Super Influential and Pretty Smart and Not Shy
A16z published
a GenAI reference architecture
in the summer of 2023. It doesnât mention RAG but RAG is the dominant AI app design pattern that it strongly implies. My issue here isnât with A16Z. They do just about as good market and product analysis as any VC firm that I know. Iâve learned a lot about GenAI and other stuff from their work.
But since they were early, aggressive, and are very influential, their weight behind vector databases and a super RAG-friendly reference architectureââEmerging LLM App Stackââchanged the trajectory of early GenAI investment toward RAG-based st

data.title: Breaking My Security Assignments
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 本文描述了作者如何通过分析虚拟机（VM）内部机制，破解其安全模块作业中的令牌获取过程。作者收到加密的更新文件（*.gpg），需要使用`installUpdate`程序解密并安装。通过分析该程序，作者发现其使用GPG解密加密的tarball文件，并需要访问`/root/.gnupg`和`/root/.vmPassphrase`文件。由于无法直接在VM中获取这些文件，作者通过挂载VM的虚拟磁盘到本地机器上，复制并更改权限，成功获取解密所需的文件。解密后，作者发现每个更新包包含一个`bin/updateVM`脚本和Java代码，用于生成和安装作业所需的令牌。最终，作者成功绕过实际操作，直接获取令牌。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：安全课程中的虚拟机（VM）保护措施及其有效性

不同观点：
• [glitchc] 认为通过VM和代码混淆进行保护不如网络边界和硬件保护有效，因为用户可以完全控制VM并绕过其访问控制。尽管加密有帮助，但由于密钥存储在VM中，因此仍是自相矛盾的安全措施。他认为，如果密钥是从服务器动态获取的，攻击会更难。同时，他指出，对于已有较高水平的学生，该课程可能没有更多可教的，建议这些学生可以学习更复杂的材料。

• [red_admiral] 对通过“黑掉”系统来完成安全作业的方式表示赞赏，认为这种方式是正确的，并建议应给予高分。他通过引用xkcd漫画来表达对这种创新解决方式的支持。

• [dmurray] 对[glitchc]的观点表示部分赞同，但指出其中的矛盾信息。一方面，[glitchc]认为已有能力的学生无需做作业，另一方面又指出这些学生仍需通过作业学习。dmurray个人认为，即便是有能力的学生仍可能从作业中受益，特别是在准备考试和积累细节知识方面。

• [Oleksii1n] 提出另一种技术性观点，建议将作业的源代码预先编译为二进制文件分发，以防止代码泄露问题，而不是在学生的实例上编译。

补充讨论：
• [glitchc] 强调了课程目标和学生能力之间的匹配问题，认为如果学生能利用高级手段完成任务，说明其已超出课程目标，课程对其可能没有更多价值。
• [dmurray] 则提醒，即便对于有能力的学生，踏实完成作业仍有其价值，尤其是在实际知识积累和考试准备方面。
• [Oleksii1n] 关注的是技术实现的细节，提出通过改变源代码分发方式来增强安全性，而不是依赖于VM和代码混淆。

争议焦点：VM和代码混淆作为保护措施的有效性以及学生是否应通过创新方式绕过这些保护来完成作业。

44258665.article_content:
Breaking my Security Assignments
A secure system broken by the fact that I can screw with a VM's internals
This post was first written in March 2024, but at the time, I was asked not to publish it for reasons that will shortly become apparent. Circumstances have changed since, so I've gone ahead and published it now with some minor alterations.
For the assignments in my security module this semester, we've been given a barebones virtual machine that we install updates into and complete assignments on. When each new assignment is released, we get given a file to download and run with this preinstalled piece of software on the VM. This sets the assignment up for us and from there we go on to solve it to get a token that can be submitted,
capture-the-flag style
. These files aren't any obviously readable type of file - they mostly look like garbage data.
But without that update file, there's no trace of the assignment on the system anywhere - which also means that those update files must contain the tokens we ned to submit and the VM must somehow be able to decrypt them... so surely we can break that for our own advantage?
Cracking Open the Updates
Having decided that I wanted to attack this the VM to try and pull out tokens without doing exercises, the first thing I turned my attention to was
installUpdate
- the program that was left on the VM for us to use to install updates. Every update file that we were given took the form
*.gpg
, so (working on the assumption that these are encrypted blobs) the logical thing to do would be to take a poke around this executable to see if there's any way to decipher how these updates are decrypted.
After getting
installUpdate
on my machine and checking that it wasn't a Bash script, I ran
strings
on it was greeted with an immediate goldmine:
$ strings installUpdate
...
/usr/bin/gpg --homedir /root/.gnupg --batch --pinentry-mode loopback --passphrase-file /root/.vmPassphrase --output %s/update.tgz --decrypt %s/updateArchive.gpg > /dev/null 2>&1
...
/usr/bin/tar zxf update.tgz > /dev/null 2>&1
...
Great! It looks like the update files are GPG encrypted tarballs. The decryption command references a
/root/.vmPassphrase
file, as well as
/root/.gnupg
that presumedly stores some keys, so it's probably a safe bet that we need both of those to do decryption.
In the VM, we don't have root
1
so I can't just boot the VM and grab the password - but I can mount its virtual disk on my local machine. Since I'm using QEMU to run the VM
2
, I can do that using these instructions:
https://unix.stackexchange.com/a/598265
The magical powers of having root on my own computer means that I can make a local copy of the VM's
/root
directory change the permissions of everything inside to be something a little more open.
With the directory in hand, some fiddling with some of the arguments in the above GPG command gives me something I can use to decrypt myself a tarball:
$ gpg --homedir root-copy/.gnupg --batch --pinentry-mode loopback --passphrase-file root-copy/.vmPassphrase --output update.tgz --decrypt ex3/update_ex3.gpg
gpg: WARNING: unsafe permissions on homedir '/media/akp/Data/Uni/S+N/root-copy/.gnupg'
gpg: encrypted with 3072-bit RSA key, ID 57ABAFF0A7DE8CC8, created 2024-01-11
"************** (Encryption key for SecNet VMs) <*****@bham.ac.uk>"
gpg: Signature made Thu 15 Feb 2024 13:12:56 GMT
gpg:                using RSA key E18EFB226702A6240F9E9A150985CE5D508F4DAE
gpg:                issuer "*****@bham.ac.uk"
gpg: Good signature from ""************** (Signing key for SecNet VMs) <*****@bham.ac.uk>" [ultimate]
gpg:                 aka ""************** <*****@bham.ac.uk>" [ultimate]
!!!!
3
Digging Around Inside
Once we extract the tarball, we're met with a few directories - the actual names of the directories vary a little bit from exercise to exercise but at the very least, they all contain a
bin
directory and a
java
directory.
As far as I can tell, each update has an "entrypoint" in the form of a shell script called
bin/updateVM
that copies and uses files in the other directories of the archive (though I can't tell if any of these directories have special meaning since I've not put any time into reversing the
installUpdate
binary).
Much of the time, the entrypoint script compiles and runs some Java code from the
java
directory. Typically there are two files present - one file always named in the form
GenTokenEx\d_2023.java
and another just called
Keys.java
. Since this is just source code
4
, a cursory poke around reveals that these files handle on-the-fly generation and installation of tokens as required by the exercises.
Some update files also reference a mysterious
systemd
service called
tokens
and, quite frankly, I can't work out why it exists. Closer inspection of the shell script that it runs shows that's it's a mechanism to
run
the Java code included in update archives, but it's also only used by (so far) 1 of 3 exercises, with the rest opting to directly run the token generation code

data.author: edwinarbus
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了在社交媒体上流行的"Loading Dance Challenge"挑战。该挑战源自说唱歌手K CAMP的歌曲《Lottery》，因其独特的舞蹈动作和节奏感迅速在TikTok等平台走红。挑战参与者需跟随音乐节奏，模仿特定的舞蹈动作，并拍摄成短视频上传。该挑战不仅吸引了大量用户参与，还推动了歌曲的再度流行。文章还提到，这类挑战展示了社交媒体在音乐推广和流行文化传播中的强大影响力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对展示项目的各种看法，包括其实际存在性、技术可行性、幽默感以及潜在的问题。

不同观点：
• [supriyo-biswas] 认为展示的项目虽然看似是个“玩笑”，但其提到曾在Recaptcha中见过类似的手势图标，并提供了链接作为证据。该用户强调这不是幻觉或网络迷因。
• [ycwatcher] 提到这个项目让他联想到歌曲《Human》的歌词，表现出对项目名称或概念的联想和幽默。
• [denysvitali] 指出该链接内容已在另一个帖子中出现过，对同一链接在24小时内被提交两次表示惊讶。
• [WD-42] 以幽默的方式建议开发一种需要做俯卧撑的验证码，以实现真正的“工作量证明” captcha。
• [cchance] 对项目表示喜爱，认为其非常有趣并引人发笑。
• [coolandsmartrr] 认为该想法有趣，但指出如果没有广角摄像头，手臂可能会被裁掉，影响用户体验。
• [phoronixrly] 讽刺地指出这种captcha可能会对残疾人造成障碍，暗示其在无障碍设计上的不足。
• [xg15] 引用了一个幽默的网络迷因“Drink Verification Can to continue”，增加了对项目玩笑性质的解读。
• [chrisco255] 表示总体上喜欢这个项目，但指出交叉手臂的示例没有成功。
• [dalemhurley] 担心这种玩笑式的想法可能会被认真对待，导致未来在视频会议中需要摆姿势验证身份。
• [yesbut] 简单直接地表示反对，但没有详细说明原因。
• [hoomanmo] 对项目是否真正有效提出疑问。
• [galuggus] 提到另一个相关网站rudecaptcha.xyz，暗示对类似玩笑或恶搞项目的关注。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点之一是项目的可行性和实用性，部分用户担心技术实现问题（如摄像头角度）以及对某些群体的潜在歧视。
- 另一个值得注意的讨论点是用户对项目幽默感的不同反应，有的认为非常有趣，有的则持怀疑或反对态度。
- 链接重复提交的问题也被提及，显示出对社区内容管理的关注。

data.title: Show HN: I built a Mac app to restore Dock-click minimize and avoid tiny buttons
data.author: goofywon
data.article_summary: Click2Minimize 是一款专为 macOS 设计的窗口管理工具，解决了苹果系统无法通过点击 Dock 图标来最小化或恢复应用的问题。它提供多种便捷操作，如点击 Dock 图标进行最小化或还原、使用鼠标滚轮切换工作空间、快速应用切换等。该软件支持 Apple Silicon 和 Intel 处理器的 Mac，兼容 macOS Sonoma 和 Sequoia，并且已经过 Apple 公证，无病毒和恶意软件。软件体积小于 1 MB，不含广告或臃肿功能，支持单用户无限设备使用（超过10台设备需获得授权）。当前版本为 v2.3.11，修复了多个问题并新增了多项手势操作功能。售价 $4.99，提供14天免费试用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一款应用的创新性、用户体验以及营销方式的讨论

不同观点：
• [yodon] 认为应用在点击组合（如左键+右键、左键+滚轮等）上的创新可能会阻碍其普及。他指出，这类组合通常未被广泛采用是因为大多数人的手部操作不适应这些方式，并以早期3D建模软件为例，说明行业已经从这种错误中吸取教训，转向使用更传统的快捷键。他建议应用应采用常规的快捷键，并允许用户自定义。

• [mattl] 讨论了该应用针对鼠标用户与触控板用户的定位，特别提到了macOS上的窗口管理问题。他认为Mac用户通常习惯于同时打开多个窗口，而Windows和Linux用户则倾向于最大化窗口。他表达了对类似Stage Manager的工具的需求，以及对更灵活的窗口管理解决方案的期望，比如结合虚拟桌面功能。

• [aspenmayer] 对应用的营销方式提出质疑，认为在Hacker News上发布需要是免费的或提供免费试用，而不是通过赠送免费许可证来获取反馈。他觉得这种方式像是在利用参与诱饵战术，并认为这种帖子不适合Hacker News。

补充讨论：
• yodon的观点中提到了早期软件设计中的错误和行业学习的过程，强调了用户体验和操作习惯在设计中的重要性。
• mattl对不同操作系统用户的行为习惯进行了对比，指出了Mac用户在窗口管理上的特殊需求，并表达了对应用在实际使用场景中表现的期望。
• aspenmayer对营销策略的质疑引发了对Hacker News社区文化和帖子适当性的讨论，提出了对透明度和无诱导性推广的要求。

争议焦点：
• 应用在点击组合上的创新是否会阻碍其普及。
• 应用的营销方式是否适合Hacker News社区以及是否应该提供免费试用。
